owner_defects: D1: cannot open the map at all from the deployed build
D2: remove fog of war — geography visible from the start, markers hidden until discovered

D1.reproduced: tools/map/player-route.mjs — real boot at `?mode=play` (rAF drives the sim), real page.keyboard presses, real touch taps. Nothing calls openMenu/stepFrames/loadState. Before the fix: M opened the inventory and the map was never reached.
D1.root_cause: UISystem.WALK_ORDER. `menu` opens the INVENTORY; `swap_right`/`swap_left` are the only way on; and `map` sat SIXTH — four presses away — with nothing anywhere in the game saying the pages turned or that a map was one of them. The surface existed and drew correctly (a visual audit had photographed it); a person could not get to it.
D1.fix: `map` moved from sixth to second in WALK_ORDER — one press from the screen `menu` opens — and the inventory's foot hint now names the page turn in the device-neutral vocabulary the rest of the interface uses (RI-JRN03 DS5: the action, never the key). RI-UIX04 Q7 is unaffected in both directions: NEVER_ADJACENT is untouched, so the journal's ring still has no `map` and the map's ring still has no `journal` (map-probe S9/S10 unchanged).
D1.instrument_trap_worth_knowing: The first three runs of the route probe reported the map unreachable even AFTER the fix would have applied, because they slept 320 ms between presses. On this box headless Chromium on a software rasteriser services requestAnimationFrame roughly once every ten seconds once a screen is up — measured with an independent rAF chain installed by the probe, with `loop.running` still true, nothing thrown, and `uiPausedFrames` freezing in step. Removing `--run-all-compositor-stages-before-draw` did not help. The probe now waits for the loop's own tick counter to advance instead of for a wall clock, and says so in the file. A fixed sleep in play mode measures the rig's frame rate and calls it a navigation defect.

D2.ruling: corpus/00-doctrine/AMENDMENT-W1-MAP-02.md — the geography whole from frame 0; place squares still earned by standing on the built pad; roads/routes still forbidden by S35, which is what keeps RI-WLD06's markerless navigation intact. Reversal is one line and §6 names three things that would overturn it.
D2.why_it_is_a_correction_not_a_preference: RI-WLD06 §5 already banned 'fog-of-war reveal-on-approach' and permitted the surface as 'paper, static, hand-drawn'. A sheet of paper does not fill in as you walk. Two items disagreed and the corpus was on the owner's side.
D2.code: game/src/ui/screens/map.js (terrain gate removed, cells_in_view counted, province-view heading corrected from 'Where I have been'); game/src/ui/system.js (the `seen` closure REMOVED rather than left unread, cells_in_view + a derived geography_always_drawn added to state().map)
D2.measured: tools/map/fog-control.mjs, head arm: 42,846 of 42,846 cells in view drawn, 0 cells in the footprint, 0 place squares — the amendment's inverted appendix test, exactly. Screenshot reports/w1-map-defects/fog-head.png.
D2.reference: corpus/70-visual/refs/morrowind/REF-A12b/REF-A12b-map__mw-*.jpg — five Morrowind map screenshots, landed by the sibling W1-MW-UI-REFS, read BEFORE building. Whole landmass out to the coast, sea a flat field, only symbols are small square markers, not one road, region name in the header. All five are late saves, so they do not settle what a fresh character's world map looks like; recorded as such in the amendment.

controls.delete_the_fix: tools/map/fog-control.mjs --arms deletefix — the one-line fog gate and the closure it needs put back on a hard-linked control clone; must turn the geography half red.
controls.null_control: --arms markers — NOT the trivial 'no map at all', which distinguishes nothing. The plausible wrong answer: `_mapPlaces()` rewritten as 'the map draws the world's sites', so the geography is whole AND every settlement is squared. Looks like a working map in a screenshot and deletes discovery from the game; must turn the marker half red.
controls.both_patches_assert_their_own_hit_count: a sabotage whose text replacement did not apply is reported as a broken arm, never as a passing control.

not_done: The phone leg of player-route.mjs had not finished when this was written; the desktop leg is the evidence for D1.

The province view reads as flat blocks of saturated region colour where Morrowind's reads as shaded relief. The height shading is applied (base_dm through shadeHex) but the palette dominates it. Out of scope for these two defects and worth a look by whoever owns map art.

The map is one press from the inventory now, but the inventory is still what `menu` opens and Escape is still eaten by pointer lock, so `KeyM` is in practice the only working menu key. Whether the map deserves its own binding is a live question and would need a HARNESS.md §4 action-set amendment.
